portable_principle: A kernel read-only lease held its captured private array; a higher-level immutable document separately owned a defensive array. The actual later document-read route used fresh lease qualification, not lease content access.

After successful defensive-document construction, explicitly retire only the lease content array. Keep the real handle, sharing, path/identity/metadata/current read permission, thread, failure state, final close and operation scope.
Explicitly retired content reads fail closed; unreleased lease content behavior is preserved. The retirement capability does not supply bytes or grant current qualification.

Account the single retained private document array rather than two arrays; keep the same256MiB cap and original publication/handle/admission limits. No eviction, early custody close, global cache or blind cap growth.

Object headers, temporary clones, parsed data, other caches, native buffers and GC timing remain outside the retained-array budget. Per-entry array removal does not establish reduced total heap peak or elapsed time.
